answer: Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. To troubleshoot the SAML login issue, please compare the assertion consumer service URL in your identity provider against the value shown on the SSO settings page. They must match exactly, including the trailing path [DOC-AUTH-003]. Additionally, inspect a failing assertion and confirm the NameID is the user's email address in lower case [DOC-AUTH-003]. If new users should be created on first login, enable just-in-time provisioning and set a default role for provisioned users [DOC-AUTH-003]. Please also ensure that just-in-time provisioning is enabled on the connection [DOC-AUTH-003]. If you have already done these steps, please let us know what you observed. We will be happy to assist you further.

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. Based on your question, it seems like you're experiencing a delay in metrics arriving at your monitoring system compared to what's shown in the console. According to our documentation, a delay of up to two minutes on metrics is expected due to aggregation before they're sent [DOC-PERF-001]. However, if the forwarded volume is higher than expected, it's likely due to debug output being forwarded, which can be resolved by applying a level filter at source [DOC-INT-002]. I recommend checking the forwarding status page to see the last successful delivery and any error returned by the destination, as well as verifying the destination credential separately if delivery has stopped entirely. Please let us know what you observed after trying these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with your environment variable not being visible to your application. To troubleshoot this, please check the scope at which the variable was defined, as service scope overrides project scope, and project scope overrides organisation defaults [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Then, review the environment overrides page, which lists values that differ from the defaults for each environment [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Finally, redeploy after changing configuration, as running containers do not pick up new values without a restart [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Please let us know what you observed after taking these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to us about your concern with secrets being printed in the logs. To address this issue, please follow these steps: Check the scope at which the variable was defined, as service scope overrides project scope, and project scope overrides organisation defaults [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Store anything sensitive as a secret rather than a variable, as secrets are masked in logs and are not readable through the API after creation [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Review the environment overrides page, which lists values that differ from the defaults for each environment [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Redeploy after changing configuration, as running containers do not pick up new values without a restart [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Additionally, please note that a secret that has been printed to logs should be treated as exposed and rotated, even if the logs are private [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. We invite you to reply with what you observed after following these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with your service's response times. To help diagnose the problem, we recommend comparing the median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page. If there's a large gap, it may indicate contention or queueing rather than a uniformly slower service [DOC-PERF-001]. Next, please check memory utilisation across instances. Sustained utilisation above eighty per cent typically shows up as latency before it shows up as failure [DOC-PERF-001]. Additionally, review the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view to identify whether the time is being spent in your service or waiting on another [DOC-PERF-001]. Finally, if load is predictable, consider adjusting the autoscaling policy to scale on request count, which responds sooner than scaling on processor utilisation [DOC-PERF-001]. Please let us know what you observe after taking these steps.

To revert to an earlier revision, please follow these steps: Open the revisions page for your service and identify the last revision that was healthy. Select roll back on that revision. Traffic will move within roughly thirty seconds and no rebuild will take place. If the release included a database migration, roll the migration back before the service, or the older code will encounter a schema it does not expect. Record the incident and the reason for the rollback before deploying a fix, while the detail is still fresh.

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. Based on the information provided, it appears that your database connection pool may be experiencing exhaustion. This can be caused by the pool size multiplied by the instance count exceeding the database connection limit, or connections not being returned to the pool after use. Long-running transactions may also be holding connections open. To troubleshoot this issue, please check the database connection pool size and ensure it is not exceeded. Additionally, verify that connections are being returned to the pool after use, and check for any long-running transactions that may be holding connections open. If the issue persists, please let us know what you have observed.

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. We understand that you're experiencing a 429 Too Many Requests error. According to our documentation [DOC-API-001], the rate limit headers returned with every response give the limit, the remaining allowance, and the reset time, which is more reliable than inferring the limit from behavior [DOC-API-001]. We recommend reading these headers to confirm the limit for your specific endpoint. Some endpoints, such as search and export endpoints, have lower limits than reads [DOC-API-001]. To implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429 responses, rather than retrying immediately, which prolongs the throttling [DOC-API-001]. If you require sustained higher throughput, you can raise the limit on your Business plan by submitting an account request [DOC-API-001].

Thank you for reaching out to us about the unclear billing period dates and unexpected charges on your invoice. To better understand your invoice and usage breakdown, please follow these steps: Open the usage breakdown for the period, which itemises charges by service and by environment [DOC-BILL-001]. Look for resources in staging or development environments, which are billed at the same rate as production [DOC-BILL-001]. Check the billing period dates at the top of the invoice. The period runs from the anniversary of the subscription date [DOC-BILL-001]. Set a usage alert on the billing page so that unexpected accrual is noticed during the period rather than at the end of it [DOC-BILL-001].

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe customer support. We're here to help you resolve the issue with unexpected overage charges. According to our documentation, unexpected overage charges can occur when the plan allowance is consumed before the end of the billing period [DOC-BILL-003]. To avoid being throttled, you can configure alerts at fifty, eighty, and ninety-five per cent of allowance rather than relying on the cap as a warning [DOC-BILL-003]. Additionally, you can decide deliberately between a hard spend cap, which stops the service, and overage, which continues at the listed rate [DOC-BILL-003]. If a spend cap has stopped a production service, an account owner can raise it immediately from the billing page and service resumes within a minute [DOC-BILL-003].

Thank you for reaching out to us. To assist you with exporting audit logs, please follow these steps: Filter the audit log by actor, resource and date range [DOC-SEC-003]. Every administrative action carries the user, the address and the outcome [DOC-SEC-003]. Note that read access to resources is not logged on Business plans, only administrative and configuration changes [DOC-SEC-003]. If the period you need is within the retention window, export the relevant period to object storage for anything needed beyond the retention window [DOC-SEC-003]. Exports are not subject to retention limits. If a policy requires retention longer than the plan provides, configure continuous export to your own storage [DOC-SEC-003]. Also, note that exports containing personal data are logged in the audit trail with the requesting user and the fields included [DOC-DATA-001]. Audit log exports are themselves audited, including the fields selected and the destination [DOC-SEC-003]. Please let us know what you observed after attempting these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with your webhook endpoint. To troubleshoot the problem, please check the webhook delivery log for the last seven days, which records every attempt with the response status and body [DOC-API-003]. This will help us understand the status of the deliveries and identify any potential issues. Additionally, please ensure that your endpoint returns a 2xx status as quickly as possible and processes the event asynchronously [DOC-API-003]. Also, verify that the signature is computed over the raw request body before any parsing [DOC-API-003]. Finally, make sure your handler is idempotent using the event identifier, as at-least-once delivery means duplicates are expected rather than exceptional [DOC-API-003]. Please let us know what you observed after taking these steps.
